records.title: Computer Science (PhD)
records.degree: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science
records.department: Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science
records.description: The Doctor of Philosophy with a major in computer science is awarded in strict conformity with the general requirements of the USC Graduate School. Departmental requirements consist of a concentrated program of study and research and a dissertation: CSCI 670, two semesters of CSCI 697, two semesters of CSCI 698 (teaching requirement) and five CSCI elective courses at the 500 level and above.

requirement_groups.name: Required courses
notes: Each student is required to complete two semesters of CSCI 697 (1 unit each, 2 maximum) and CSCI 670 (4 units).
The CSCI 670 course requirement may be waived by examination only. The owner of CSCI 670 is in charge of creating and grading the waiver examination.
CSCI 697 and CSCI 698 may not be waived.

requirement_groups.name: Teaching requirement
notes: Students are required to pass two semesters of CSCI 698 (1-2 units each, no maximum) as part of a teaching requirement.

requirement_groups.name: Elective courses
requirement_groups.options_rule: CSCI courses at the 500 level and above, 4 units each; no more than two (8 units) at the 500 level, the rest at the 600 level.
notes: Each student must complete five CSCI courses at the 500 level and above, 4 units each.
No more than two of these courses (8 units total) may be at the 500 level; the remaining must be CSCI courses at the 600 level.
Directed Research units or thesis credits do not satisfy this requirement.
Students are strongly advised to take at least one of their elective courses in an area of computer science that is different from their proposed area of research.

limits.text: No more than two elective courses (8 units total) may be at the 500 level.

records.other_requirements: Consult the department's separately published guide for the screening procedure, the teaching requirement, the qualifying examination, the thesis proposal and other requirements.

notes: At least 60 units, at least 40 of which must be at the 500 level or above.
Students must maintain a 3.0 GPA to remain in good academic standing.
A master's degree is not required for entry; a four-year bachelor's degree in a relevant field is.
Up to 8 units of CSCI 699 may be applied to course requirements.
Every student must TA for two semesters, including at least one undergraduate class.
Attend four department seminars and/or PhD thesis proposals each semester.
Biannual review each fall and spring; two consecutive 'Below expectations' ratings may be grounds for removal.

Qualifying exam: written paper (at least 15 pages, ACM style, at least 30 references) and oral presentation within 60 days; each part may be retaken once. Should be taken in the 4th semester and passed within four years of admission.
Thesis proposal must be made by the end of the 5th year (end of 4th year strongly recommended).
Dissertation defense within seven years of admission (six with a relevant master's).
After passing the qualifying exam, enroll in CSCI 794A and register continuously in 794 each fall and spring; CSCI 794A and 794B are the minimum before the degree.
Students can petition for the MS in Computer Science en route to the PhD.
